h: Judging Ourselves Through the Gates of Torah and Fear

p: שׁוֹפְטִים וְשׁוֹטְרִים תִּתֶּן לְךָ בְּכָל שְׁעָרֶיךָ
"Judges and officers you shall appoint for yourself in all your gates
אֲשֶׁר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נוֹתֵן לְךָ לִשְׁבָטֶיךָ
which Hashem your God gives you, according to your tribes,
בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ה, ה)
In Midrash Rabbah on this parshah (Devarim Rabbah 5:5):
that the officer be like the judge,
in place of the stick and the strap,
and the one who strikes should not himself need to be flogged."
that the judge should rebuke himself, etc.,
and this will stand for him
in place of the stick and strap.
And this is the meaning of "Judges and officers
you shall appoint for yourself" — for yourself:
that one should be a judge and an officer to himself.
into "the heart of the wise man at his right";
and "officer" is against "the heart of the fool" (Koheles 10:2),
that there is a stick and a strap.
And this is to be like an officer to himself:
to set before himself the fear of punishment,
and to make fences for himself
against the heart of the fool.
And likewise it is expounded in the Tanchuma (on this parshah, 3):
"'Judges and officers you shall appoint for yourself'
that there should not be in them
שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בַּשּׁוֹפֵט דָּבָר שֶׁל פְּסוֹלֶת
that there should be nothing unfit in the judge;
דָּרַשׁ גַּם כֵּן תִּתֶּן לְךָ לְעַצְמְךָ
it too expounded "for yourself" as "for your own self."
קָאֵי מִצְוָה זוֹ עַל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
this mitzvah applies to every one of Yisrael,
to be a judge and officer to himself;
so from where do we learn
that it refers to judges and magistrates?
But from what is said afterward:
"and they shall judge the people," etc.
that is, one who will be
a judge and officer to himself
יוּכַל לִשְׁפּוֹט אֶת הָעָם גַּם כֵּן
will be able to judge the people as well.
But according to this explanation one must understand
the words "in all your gates," etc.,
עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת לא, ב)
according to what they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 31b):
"Any person who has Torah in him
but has no fear of Heaven
who was given the inner keys
but was not given the outer keys:
and Torah to the inner keys;
and since it used the term "keys,"
(הַקְדָּמָה, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל דַּרְגָּא חֲמִישָׁאָה, ה, א)
there the Yud is the fear of Hashem,
the Yud of Havayah is Chochmah,
and the four letters of this Name
That is, the Torah is called by the Name Havayah,
regarding the blessing before the Torah,
"When I call the Name of Hashem,
and this is the gate of Torah.
And the Name Adnut indicates fear,
"And if I am a master, where is My fear?"
וְכֵן מִדַּת מַלְכוּת מוֹרֶה עַל יִרְאָה
And likewise the attribute of Malchus indicates fear;
and this is the gate of fear of Heaven.
עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּשְׁנָה (פֶּרֶק ג דְּאָבוֹת)
regarding what they said in the Mishnah (Avos 3:9):
"And whoever's wisdom precedes his fear of sin
only that it does not endure;
"Why is there a price in the hand of a fool
to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?"
as referring to Torah scholars who study Torah
but have no fear of Heaven;
הֲרֵי דְּמִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
so one who has no fear of Heaven
does it call it by the name wisdom?
"A person should always engage in Torah," etc.,
for from not for its own sake he comes to for its own sake";
"One who does it not for its own sake
it would have been better for him not to have been created."
"Whoever engages in Torah not for its own sake,
it becomes for him a deadly poison";
between kinds of "not for its own sake."
And Rabbeinu Chaim Or Zarua explained
for having learned not for its own sake,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לוֹ שָׂכָר עַל הַלִּימּוּד
and nevertheless he has reward for the learning,
since it leads to for its own sake.
It is similar to what Tosafos wrote (Taanis 11a)
that according to Shmuel he is called a sinner:
and similar to what they said
about one who fasts a dream-fast on Shabbos,
that his decree is torn up,
and he must fast again for his fast.
Therefore in the Mishnah, which used the words
"his wisdom precedes his fear of sin"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא לִידֵי יִרְאָה
that is, afterward he comes to fear,
only that the wisdom preceded it
that his wisdom does not endure:
this wisdom does not yet endure,
and nevertheless it leads to for its own sake,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִי שֶׁעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
Which is not so with one who engages in Torah
and has no fear of Heaven,
who has not come to fear at all;
"Why is there a price in the hand of a fool,"
for this is not at all within the category of wisdom.
And likewise we find that it is written (Yeshayahu 55:1):
"Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the water,"
which is expounded in the Gemara (Taanis 7a)
as referring to a student who is not worthy,
for of a worthy student it is written:
"Whoever teaches a student who is not worthy
"is like one who throws a stone," etc.
that they warn not to teach
a student who is not worthy;
but to the student himself they say
that although it is not yet in his power
to refine his heart so as to be worthy
and learn in order to do
and has a longing for the Torah,
let him compel himself to go and learn,
and then Hashem Yisbarach will grant him
that he come to for its own sake.
And although they will punish him for the learning
and this wisdom will not endure in his hand,
nevertheless this learning will bring him
afterward to for its own sake,
and he will refine his heart,
and his fear of sin will precede his wisdom,
"Just as there is no Torah without fear,
אוּף הָכִי לֵית דְּחִילוּ בְּלָא אוֹרַיְיתָא וְכוּלֵּי
so too there is no fear without Torah," etc.;
דְּאִי בַּר נָשׁ לָא יָדַע אוֹרַיְיתָא
"For if a person does not know the Torah,
and the reward of its commandments,
'nor can an unlearned man be pious,'
and 'an ignoramus cannot fear sin,'" etc.;
וְכֵן בַּמִּשְׁנָה גַּם כֵּן (אָבוֹת ג, יז)
and likewise in the Mishnah too (Avos 3:17):
"If there is no wisdom, there is no fear;
if there is no fear," etc.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת שָׁם)
And this is according to what they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 31b)
Woe to one who has no courtyard
but makes a gate for the courtyard";
that the Torah is only a gate
through which to enter fear of Heaven;
לְכָךְ צָרִיךְ שֶׁתַּקְדִּים לוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
therefore he must first have fear of Heaven;
there are two levels of fear:
for it is stated in the holy Zohar (Bereishis, I 5b):
and in the holy Zohar (there, I 11b):
and of one who has no fear of Heaven
it said, "when he has no heart,"
and he is called a fool.
And this is called the outer keys,
וְהֵם ד׳ אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁל שֵׁם אדנ״י
and they are the four letters of the Name Adnut.
Only, the Torah is also called
that the fear enter the depths of the heart,
"Then you shall understand the fear of Hashem,
and find the knowledge of God"
which is the aspect of Binah;
into the depths of the heart;
and the Torah is the gate to this,
and it is the inner keys,
which are the four letters of Havayah.
And this is the meaning of
שׁוֹפְטִים וְשׁוֹטְרִים תִּתֶּן לְךָ בְּכָל שְׁעָרֶיךָ
"Judges and officers you shall appoint for yourself in all your gates":
that is, in the two gates,
in the gates of Torah and the gates of fear,
to bring the words of Torah into the heart,
and this will be in place of the stick and the strap.

Two Levels of Fear and Their Gates

p: אֲשֶׁר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נוֹתֵן לְךָ לִשְׁבָטֶיךָ
"which Hashem your God gives you, according to your tribes,"
there are twelve permutations, as is known,
and the holy Ari arranged them
for the twelve months of the year,
so that to each month belongs
a specific permutation of the Name
there is a specific innovation in words of Torah,
the aspect of the moon that receives from the sun;
as we said on what is said
"This is the burnt-offering of each month in its month":
שֶׁכָּל חוֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת
that each month has a specific holiness,
and corresponding to it a specific permutation.
שְׁבָטִים עַל סִדְרוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי
"The tribes are according to the order of the world," etc.,
"and likewise the constellations and the months."
of the permutations of the Name Havayah,
pertaining to the holiness of that tribe.
that the tribes are the aspect of
the moon that receives from the sun;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סח, י)
"Who revealed to him that my name is Sun?"
And he is a chariot for the Name Havayah, as is known.
And the tribes are the moon,
וְכָל שֵׁבֶט יֵשׁ לוֹ צֵירוּף מְיוּחָד
and each tribe has a specific permutation
through which it receives the words of Torah
from this permutation of the Name Havayah,
שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
which is the Name of the Torah, as mentioned above.
as they said (in Sefer Yetzirah, chapter 4):
הַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן ב׳ פְּעָמִים י״ב
that is, also two times twelve.
And this is according to what was mentioned above,
that there are two levels of fear:
a fear that is called a gate,
"a gate to enter into the faith,"
for which the Torah is the gate.
two permutations of the Name Adnut,
which indicates fear, as mentioned above,
And this is the meaning of
"you shall appoint for yourself in all your gates
אֲשֶׁר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נוֹתֵן לְךָ לִשְׁבָטֶיךָ
which Hashem your God gives you, according to your tribes":
שֶׁכָּל שֵׁבֶט יֵשׁ לוֹ צֵירוּף מְיוּחָד
that each tribe has a specific permutation
in Torah and in fear of Heaven;
and the four letters of the two Names
"and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment";
for it is not enough that you appoint for yourself
judges and officers for yourself alone;
רַק צָרִיךְ לְזַכּוֹת אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ גַּם כֵּן
rather one must bring merit to his fellow too,
for all of Yisrael are guarantors for one another (Shevuos 39a).
And in the Midrash (Tanchuma on this parshah)
אָמַר שֶׁיְּהֵא מַטִּין אֶת הָעָם לְכַף צֶדֶק
it says that they should incline the people toward the scale of merit;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְזַכּוֹת לְהָעָם גַּם כֵּן
that is, one must bring merit to the people as well.
that they should incline and plead merit for them
before the Holy One, blessed be He.
וְהוּא שֶׁמִּי שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹפֵט וְשׁוֹטֵר לְעַצְמוֹ
That is, one who is a judge and officer to himself
can plead merit for the community,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מט, ט)
about Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him:
and likewise it is expounded in the Pesikta (on this haftarah)
And one who is a judge and officer to himself
can draw down upon the generation bounty
for according to all, the Torah was given on Shabbos
and all of Yisrael are called
יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי שׁוֹמְרֵי שַׁבָּת (תַּעֲנִית ח, ב)
"those who fear My Name," keepers of Shabbos (Taanis 8b)
this is the gate of Torah and the gate of fear,
and they can draw down blessing and bounty
